exercises.title: Traffic stop for a stop sign violation
narrative: At 2315 hours you see a sedan roll through a stop sign at Oak Street and 3rd Avenue without stopping. The road is dry and lit.
You activate your lights and the driver pulls over right away. The driver hands you a license and says they were looking for an address. You smell no odor of alcohol and observe normal speech.
You check the license and registration. Both are valid. You issue a written warning and explain it. The driver thanks you and leaves at 2324 hours.

statements.text: The road surface was dry and the intersection was lit.
The vehicle did not stop at the stop sign at Oak Street and 3rd Avenue at about 2315 hours.
The driver was visibly intoxicated.
The vehicle was speeding at 25 over the limit.
The driver produced a valid license and the registration was valid.
The driver said they were looking for an address.
The driver was cited and the vehicle was towed.
The driver was issued a written warning.
The driver became aggressive and had to be restrained.
The driver had normal speech and no odor of alcohol was noted.

exercises.title: Shoplifting at a retail store
narrative: Dispatch sends you to a retail store where loss prevention staff are holding a man in a back office. The employee says they watched him put two items in his bag and leave the register area without paying.
You view the store video and see the man place the items in his bag. The man says he forgot to pay. The items are worth about 38 dollars in total. The man has a valid ID and no weapons.
The store wants the man trespassed. You issue a trespass notice and a citation, and the items are returned to the shelf.

statements.text: The man said he forgot to pay.
Loss prevention reported seeing the man conceal two items and leave the register area without paying.
The man pulled a knife on loss prevention.
The man fled and was caught after a foot pursuit.
The store video showed the man placing the items in his bag.
The man had a valid ID and was searched with no weapons found.
The items were valued at over 5,000 dollars.
The total value of the items was about 38 dollars.
The store declined to provide video.
The man was issued a trespass notice and a citation.

exercises.title: Domestic disturbance between two adults
narrative: You arrive at an apartment after a neighbor calls about shouting. You hear a raised voice, then silence as you knock. A woman opens the door and a man is seated in the living room.

You separate them to speak privately. The woman says they argued about money, there was no physical contact, and she is not afraid. The man agrees the argument was verbal. You see no injuries, damage or weapons, and children are asleep in a bedroom.
Both adults decline to press charges. You give them resource information. The man agrees to stay with a friend for the night and leaves at 0040 hours.

statements.text: A neighbor made the original call about shouting.
Both parties said the argument was verbal only and there was no physical contact.
The woman had visible bruises on her arms.
A firearm was seized from the apartment.
No injuries, damage or weapons were observed at the apartment.
Two children were asleep in a bedroom.
The man was arrested for assault.
The parties were interviewed separately.
The man refused to leave and had to be removed with force.
The man agreed to leave and stay elsewhere for the night.

exercises.title: Residential burglary report
narrative: A homeowner returns from work and finds a rear window broken and the back door open. The homeowner says nobody had permission to enter.

You clear the house with no one inside. The homeowner reports a laptop and a jewelry box missing. You photograph the broken window and see shoe prints in the flower bed. A neighbor saw a dark van parked on the street at midday but did not see a plate.
You call for a crime scene technician, who lifts prints from the window frame. You give the homeowner a report number and advice on securing the window.

statements.text: Shoe prints were noticed in the flower bed.
The rear window was broken and the back door was open when the homeowner returned.
The suspect was seen leaving by a witness who identified him by name.
The house was found to be occupied by an unknown person.
A laptop and a jewelry box were reported missing.
The homeowner was given a report number.
A television and a car were also stolen.
A neighbor saw a dark van on the street at midday but no plate was seen.
Nothing was photographed at the scene.
A crime scene technician collected prints from the window frame.

exercises.title: Two vehicle collision at an intersection
narrative: You respond to a collision at a signalized intersection. Vehicle 1 is a pickup truck and vehicle 2 is a small hatchback. Both drivers are standing outside their vehicles.

The hatchback driver says the light was green when she entered. The pickup driver says his light was green as well. A witness at the bus stop says the pickup entered on a red light. The hatchback driver reports neck pain and is checked by medics, and she declines transport. The pickup has front damage and the hatchback has damage on the driver side.
You document the debris, measure skid marks, and issue the pickup driver a citation for failure to obey a signal.

statements.text: Both drivers said their light was green.
A witness said the pickup entered the intersection on a red light.
The hatchback driver was transported in critical condition.
The collision happened on a highway with no signals.
The hatchback driver reported neck pain and declined transport after being checked by medics.
Skid marks were measured and debris was documented.
Both drivers were arrested for impaired driving.
The pickup had front damage and the hatchback had driver side damage.
The witness said they did not see the collision.
The pickup driver was cited for failure to obey a traffic signal.

exercises.title: Welfare check on an elderly resident
narrative: A family member in another city asks for a check on an elderly man who has not answered his phone for two days. You arrive and knock on his door and call his name with no answer.

You see a newspaper pile on the porch and a light on inside. A neighbor says she last saw him three days ago. With your supervisor's approval, and with exigency based on the risk to his health, you enter through an unlocked rear door.
You find the man on the kitchen floor, conscious but unable to stand. Medics treat him and take him to the hospital. You notify the family member by phone.

statements.text: A neighbor last saw him three days earlier.
The resident had not answered his phone for two days, according to the family member.
The man was found deceased at the scene.
The man refused all help and you left.
You entered through an unlocked rear door because of a concern for his health.
The family member was notified by phone afterward.
You forced the front door open with a ram.
